name: Palladium
occurrence: Found in nickel-copper ores and platinum-group deposits; also recycled significantly from old catalytic converters.
majorUses: Hydrogen purification and storage (absorbs up to 900 times its own volume of H₂)
notableCharacteristics: Can absorb an extraordinary volume of hydrogen gas into its metal lattice, making it useful for hydrogen storage and purification research.
whyHere: With a fully-filled 4d¹⁰ subshell and empty 5s orbital, palladium's unusual electron gaps let hydrogen atoms slip into its metal lattice easily, explaining its record-setting hydrogen absorption capacity.
didYouKnow: A palm-sized block of palladium can absorb enough hydrogen gas to fill nearly 900 times its own volume, a property researchers are actively exploring for future hydrogen fuel storage.
genZNote: Basically a hydrogen sponge disguised as a precious metal. Also cleans up your car's exhaust while it's at it.
